work.abstract_text: Question 2.32 on page 14 of Remi Salinas Schmeis's General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into ω-Chains (arXiv:2610.29056v1, 2026) asks whether every poset has an ω-chain-partitionable extension that order-embeds into every such extension. We answer negatively: even a two-element antichain has no such extension. Two countable extensions force incompatible behavior for upper bounds of incomparable elements. The same argument gives the connected three-element fork as a counterexample and, by order duality, the corresponding negative answer for ω*-chains. More generally, a nonempty countable poset of bounded finite height has such a least extension if and only if it has a greatest element. Every poset has a partitionable extension, even with ω replaced by any nonzero ordinal.

work.title: Bounded-height classification for Salinas Schmeis's ω-chain extension question
